options.title: Body sensor
options.help: What sees the dancer. The game was made for the Kinect v1. With a webcam (or any camera Windows sees) the project's own sensor turns the picture into a Kinect skeleton: no app to install or open, everything ships in mods/webcam. Calibrate camera... sets it up; Sensor preview... shows what the game will see.

values.label: Kinect (original)
values.help: Microsoft's Kinect runtime, as the game ships.

values.label: Webcam or any camera
values.help: The whole body must be in the picture, feet included, as with the Kinect. Calibrate camera... once where you play (about a minute, nothing typed). Windows Studio Effects are turned off for the session where the camera allows it.

options.title: Webcam sensor runs on
options.help: Only with the webcam as Body sensor. Where its main network runs. The GPU ran the sensor better in every test (faster, lower latency, and the CPU left to the game); on a PC where the GPU cannot run it, the sensor falls back to the CPU by itself. The CPU by hand only to compare.

values.label: GPU (DirectML; the CPU if the GPU cannot run it)

options.title: Language
options.help: The language of every text and menu picture the game draws. The machine picks one at the factory. A fourth code in the game (kan, Simplified Chinese, from the Mainland China version) is not offered: Konami never shipped its pictures, and the game crashes looking for them.

values.label: Chinese (Traditional)
values.help: The game's own Traditional Chinese assets (*_lang_han).

options.title: Song list
options.help: Konami's August 2016 offline build locked 22 songs and emptied the audio of 20 of them (licences expiring). This brings them back.

values.label: Original (80 songs)
values.help: The song list as Konami shipped it.

values.label: Every song unlocked (102 songs)
values.help: The 22 locked songs unlocked; the 20 emptied audio banks restored (14 are Konami's own audio, as in its October 2015 build; 6 are found only in a 2017 copy of the February 2016 build, who put them there is not known: brav iron maru merr noff rena); Konami's typo in rena's second chart fixed; YESTERDAY, its chart from the Dance Masters disc, its audio and jacket from that same 2017 copy; and the song-select preview of every song that had none, cut at the instant Konami chose for the others.

options.title: Song titles in English
options.help: In English the song list still shows Japanese titles and artists. This writes them with their official English or romanised names (from the releases and the BEMANI references), so a player can read them and look them up.

options.title: Stealth difficulty
options.help: Stealth is the hardest chart played with no step markers. For the 30 songs that came from the Dance Masters disc it copies EXTREME, because the disc had no master chart; this makes it copy MASTER, as the arcade's own songs do.

options.title: Ranking event icon
options.help: When a server runs a ranking event (two songs everyone competes on), the game was meant to mark those songs' difficulties with a RANKING! icon in the difficulty select, but never did: Konami's build does not load the file that holds the picture. This loads it. Nothing is drawn without an event.

values.label: RANKING! icon on the event's songs

options.title: Game mode
options.help: How a game is paid and timed, set as the arcade's operator sets it in the service menu (free play in COIN OPTIONS, then EVENT MODE): the same state, written for you. Original: your game's settings stay as they are. Credits: coins, as the arcade. Free play: the same game without credits. Event mode, the operator setting for shows and parties: free play with the clocks frozen (no time limit, no game over between songs); the arcade switches it off at every boot, this keeps it on. Credits and Free play are saved in your game's settings, so Original afterwards keeps the last one.

options.title: Songs per game
options.help: How many songs a game gives before the title, whatever the service menu's STAGE setting holds. Original: the service menu's (Konami's is 2, 3 when the e-amusement extra stage applies). At most 4: the game keeps 4 stage records per player.

options.title: Resolution
options.help: The game renders at 1280x720. The others render natively: 3D, effects and 2D, the camera picture included; not an upscale of the 720p image. Only the modes your main screen offers are listed, since the game always runs in exclusive full screen (a higher one needs that monitor, or AMD VSR / NVIDIA DSR switched on).

options.title: Frame rate
options.help: Vsync is always on: the game never draws more frames than your monitor can show, and the songs run on real time, so they stay in sync at any frame rate. What each PC does depends on its monitor and on Windows, so if one choice does not give you what it says, try another. Before playing, close Task Manager and anything set to stay on top, on any screen: Windows then has to compose the screen, and frames get lost. You never need to change your monitor's Hz.

values.label: Original: what Konami's game asks for
values.help: Nothing changed: the game asks for 60 Hz. It may run at 60 fps or faster, depending on the PC; above 60 the song select runs fast. If you want more frames and stay at 60, choose Unlimited.

values.label: Unlimited: up to your monitor's maximum
values.help: Asks for your monitor's highest refresh rate: as many frames as the PC can draw, up to that. The song and difficulty select keep the cabinet's speed (Konami's step once per frame, so above 60 they run faster). If the picture jumps because the PC cannot keep up, or the PC gets hot, choose Limit to 60.

values.label: Limit to 60 fps
values.help: Never more than 60, whatever the PC could do: less heat and more power left over. Stability over frames: for when Unlimited and the webcam sensor together give you trouble, and for notebooks.

options.title: Anti-aliasing
options.help: Smooths the jagged edges of the 3D (SMAA, about 1.4 ms per frame).

options.title: Texture filtering
options.help: Keeps floors and walls sharp at a glancing angle (anisotropic x16, about 0.4 ms).

options.title: Sound memory
options.help: Raises the game's sound memory from 76 to 128 MB. Needed by the unlocked songs' previews (they do not fit in 76 MB and then no sound plays at all).
options.sector: Support (switched on by the options that need it)

options.title: Sound files
options.help: The game reads its music and sound banks straight from data/sound, where mods cannot reach. Mods that bring audio (restored songs, previews, YESTERDAY) make it read mods/snd instead, where the launcher links every original bank plus theirs.
options.sector: Support (switched on by the options that need it)

options.title: Memory limit
options.help: Lets the 32-bit game use 4 GB of address space instead of 2: with 2 GB it runs out of memory on a modern PC and crashes. Set on the launcher's copy of spice.exe, never on yours.
options.sector: Support (switched on by the options that need it)

options.title: Attract demo: difficulty
options.help: The demo the cabinet plays while idle. Original: standard charts.

options.title: Attract demo: length
options.help: Original: each demo song stops after 30 seconds.

options.title: Attract demo: song order
options.help: Original: two hand-picked playlists (50 songs).

values.label: Every song, shuffled, none twice per round

options.title: Attract demo: score display
options.help: Shows the SCORE bar and the COMBO during the demo, as in real play.

values.label: Score and combo
values.help: No camera picture in the demo (verified with a sensor connected).

options.title: Render threads
options.help: The PC build prepares each frame on ONE worker thread. This sizes the pool for your CPU at boot (CPUs - 2, between 1 and 4): smoother songs on a fast monitor.

options.title: Diagnostic log
options.help: To report a crash, a problem or how the webcam sensor did: the game, spice2x and every mod log what they do, and when the game closes a report is saved in mods\reports (your Windows user and PC names removed). Send that zip back. Slower to start; leave it off to play.
